item.title: Johnson To Start, Rohl On The Bench | 4-2-3-1 Everton Predicted Lineup Vs Arsenal
item.description: Johnson To Start, Rohl On The Bench | 4-2-3-1 Everton Predicted Lineup Vs Arsenal Everton will face off against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium this Saturday as they look to secure a result on the road in the Premier League. The Toffees suffered a 2-0 loss at the hands of Chelsea recently, so they would be eager to put in a much-improved showing this weekend. David Moyes will set his men up in a 4-2-3-1 formation and is expected to make one change to his first XI for this game. Brennan Johnson could play from the start of this clash, while Merlin Rohl makes way for him and drops to the bench. 4-2-3-1 Everton Predicted Lineup To Face Arsenal Defence Jordan Pickford will operate in goal for the Merseyside club after conceding two goals in his last outing. James Tarkowski will play alongside Jarrad Branthwaite at the centre of the Everton backline as they look to keep a good shape at the back throughout the 90 minutes. Ainsley Maitland-Niles will try to catch the eye as the right-back, while Vitaliy Mykolenko hopes to prove his worth on the other flank as the left-back. Both of them will have to perform their defensive duties well before trying to offer support to their teammates up top. Jake O’Brien will offer cover for the centre-back positions on the bench. LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 17: James Tarkowski of Everton reacts as players of Chelsea confront Referee Paul Tierney during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Everton and Chelsea FC at Hill Dickinson Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Molly Darlington/Getty Images) Midfield Harrison Armstrong and James Garner will operate as Moyes’ holding midfielders as they try to make life tough for the home side in the middle of the park. The gifted trio of Jack Grealish, Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Brennan Johnson will play just ahead of them as part of the Everton attack. All three of them need to be at their best if the Toffees want to stand a chance of securing a good result at the Emirates this weekend. Christian Norgaard and Hayden Hackney will make up the numbers on the bench and might come on to make an impact in the second 45 minutes if required. Attack Thierno Barry will lead the charge for the Merseyside outfit on the offensive end of the field. He would be eager to get his name on the scoresheet versus the Gunners this Saturday. Tyrique George will have to settle for a spot on the bench as he waits for his chance to influence the game in the final quarter if needed.

item.title: Como president reveals how Fabrizio Romano helped them sign Martin Baturina
item.description: Como president reveals how Fabrizio Romano helped them sign Martin Baturina Serie A side Como picked up a huge 4-1 win over Manchester United on Thursday and the result will live long in the memory of Italian football fans. Martin Baturina starred in the tie and their president has now opened up about how the Croatian was signed by the lakeside club. The attacker has become one of Como’s most important players this season, having joined in the summer of 2025 from Dinamo Zagreb. He has already been linked with a host of clubs across Europe and club president Mirwan Suwarso has now revealed what led to the deal. Suwarso spoke to LNS journalist Hanif Thamrin and he was aksed about the background on the Baturina deal, as he revealed Fabrizio Romano’s role. Suwarso said- via Calciomercato : “Baturina signed thanks to Football Manager? No, it didn’t exactly happen that way. “Actually, Fabrizio Romano recommended Baturina to me. One day he said, ‘Are you interested in meeting this player?’ I replied, ‘Who is he? I don’t know him.’ He explained that there was an agent interested in meeting me. I don’t normally meet agents, but I asked who it was. When I heard the name Baturina, it sounded familiar.” This led to Suwarso asking his data team to assess Baturina further. “So I asked our data department to study him. They replied, “We don’t even need to look at the numbers; we already know who he is.” But I insisted, “Check it out anyway.” He was playing for Dinamo Zagreb, and I wanted to see if he’d be able to adapt quickly to Serie A.” Suwarso also disclosed that current Inter star Petar Sucic was Como’s initial target but a deal for him never worked out. “Actually, the player we initially wanted to buy was Petar Sucic. Yes, the Inter player. We had already reached an agreement with Dinamo Zagreb for him. I don’t remember all the details of that period, but we had an agreement with the club. The problem was that the commissions requested by the agents were almost equal to the price of the player’s transfer, and at that point we said it didn’t make sense to continue.” “Sucic went to Inter and we had the opportunity to sign Baturina. We were actually looking for a player with more of Sucic’s characteristics, a number 8. But Baturina represented an interesting opportunity. We studied the data, it was all positive, and we decided to proceed.” Decision paying off Baturina’s versatility and ability to roam freely in attack seems to really suit Cesc Fabregas’ side. It also brings the most out of him, which is why many top clubs are also after his signature. So even if Como didn’t initially want Baturina, it is all going in the right direction. Kaustubh Pandey – GIFN

item.title: Siena's league adds fellow New York school Le Moyne for 2027-28
item.description: Siena and Le Moyne, shown playing an exhibition game in Loudonville in 2017, will become Metro Conference rivals when the Dolphins join the league for the 2027-28 season. (Robert Dungan) Beginning next year, Siena University will have a new rival in the Metro Conference. The Metro announced Thursday that Le Moyne College, located in Syracuse, has accepted an invitation to join the conference as a full member for the 2027-28 academic year. Le Moyne will officially join on July 1, 2027, increasing the Metro to 13 full member institutions. The Dolphins effectively replace Fairfield, which is leaving the Metro to join the Coastal Athletic Association at the conclusion of the 2026-27 academic year. Le Moyne is leaving the Northeast Conference, to which the Dolphins have belonged since upgrading from Division II to Division I in all sports in 2023. Le Moyne, a Jesuit institution, previously competed in the Metro as an associate member in baseball for 18 years and women's lacrosse for nine seasons. "We are excited to welcome Le Moyne College back to the Metro Conference," Metro Commissioner Travis Tellitocci said in a news release. "Le Moyne's leadership has taken an aggressive approach to building its Division I athletics program and demonstrated a strong commitment to investing in its future success." Siena president Chuck Seifert welcomed Le Moyne on behalf of the Metro Council of Presidents. "Le Moyne is an outstanding institution that shares our foundational commitment to academic excellence, integrity, and holistic student-athlete development," Seifert said in the news release. "Their rich tradition and momentum in Division I athletics make them a natural fit for our Conference, and their Catholic and faith-based tradition further enriches the values-driven identity of our league." Le Moyne men's basketball went 15-17 overall and 10-8 in the NEC last season under head coach Nate Champion. The women's basketball team was 12-21 and 9-9 for head coach Nick DiPillo. Their teams will be eligible for the Metro's automatic bids to the NCAA Tournament. Le Moyne completed an accelerated Division I transition in June 2026 to earn full NCAA Division I active member status. Siena men's basketball last played Le Moyne during the regular season in the 1992-93 season. The Dolphins hold a 39-23 lead the all-time rivalry, though Siena has won all six regular-season meetings since upgrading to Division I in 1976-77. Le Moyne upset Siena 73-71 in an exhibition game in Loudonville on Nov. 4, 2017. Subscribe There’s more to Albany with the Times Union. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Erin Andrews Gushes Over ‘Wonderful’ Josh Allen, Says He Makes Her Smile ‘So Hard’ Her ‘Face Hurts’
item.description: ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA; BONNIE CASH/UPI/Newscom/The Mega Agency Josh Allen certainly has a fan in Erin Andrews ! During the Wednesday, October 21, episode of her and Charissa Thompson ‘s Calm Down podcast, the sports commentator, 48, reflected on her recent sit-down interview with the Buffalo Bills quarterback, 30, which aired on FOX NFL Sunday on October 18. “What a dream. Can I just say, you and I always talk about how fortunate we are with these guys giving us their time, but it was a week that he was away with his team,” Erin explained. “They were kind of treating it like a training camp vibe, breaking bread, as he would say, going out.” Jason Pohuski/Cal Sport Media/Newscom/The Mega Agency The former Dancing with the Stars host pointed out that Allen — who tied the knot with Hailee Steinfeld in 2025, and shares 6-month-old daughter Harper with the actress, 29 — was generous enough to give her his time in California after the Bills’ win against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on Monday, October 12. “The fact that they came out, they came off the win versus L.A., and they were going to hunker down and go over some things here heading into Week 6, and he was like, ‘Yeah, I’ll do the sit down’. Come on, Josh Allen. You are so sweet,” she gushed. “I was so appreciative … and I really am grateful for that.” “How do you not like him? I just smile,” Andrews added before joking about her cosmetic injections: “My Botox is gone when I listen to him because I’m smiling so hard my face hurts.” ZUMAPRESS.com / MEGA “He’s so just absolutely so wonderful to be around. I was going to say adorable, but I can see the headline. ‘Erin Andrews calls Josh Allen adorable’, but he’s adorable,” Andrews admitted. In his interview with Andrews, the NFL star got personal, admitting he’s “softer” and “more emotional” since he and Steinfeld, 29, welcomed their first child together. “I look at her, and it’s just like sometimes I just wanna cry. It’s just like, that’s my daughter, that’s my baby. item.description: UEL | Juventus 2-2 Rennes: Woltemade rescues a point for troubled Old Lady Juventus fought back for a 2-2 draw with Stade Rennais, as Nick Woltemade converted a penalty and provided the assist for Zeki Celik, but Jhon Lucumi’s late winner was disallowed. The Bianconeri were in dismal Serie A form coming off a 3-0 home defeat to Lazio, yet boasted a 100 per cent Europa League record after beating NEC 5-0 and completing a comeback 2-1 win away to Celta Vigo . Francisco Conceicao, Kenan Yildiz, Manuel Locatelli, Jeff Ekhator and Kamil Grabara were injured, with Edon Zhegrova off the UEFA list. For the first time, Nick Woltemade and Randal Kolo Muani were started together. Rennes missed top scorer Esteban Lepaul with an ankle injury and switched to a three-man defence after a draw at Sturm Graz and 2-1 win over OFI Crete. See how it all unfolded on the Liveblog. However, Rennes responded quickly as Bryan Reynolds was allowed to knock back a cross to the far post, finding Musa Al-Taamari to turn in from six yards and draw level. Federico Gatti’s header was palmed away by a sensational Samba save from close range, but Weston McKennie had a remarkable double chance to score. First he was denied by Samba’s save, then somehow hit the upright on the rebound from point-blank range. Burrow’s Past Comments Burrow has never publicly aligned himself with either political party or offered a strong political endorsement. That said, he certainly hasn’t been afraid to share controversial political stances, either. In 2020, during the protests that followed the murder of George Floyd, Burrow made it clear that he stood with the Black community. “The Black community needs our help,” Burrow wrote in a post . “They have been unheard for far too long. I’m pro-Susan who was sexually assaulted on her way home from work, only to come to the horrific realization that her assailant planted his seed in her when she got a positive pregnancy test result a month later. I’m pro-Theresa who hemorrhaged due to a placental abruption, causing her parents, spouse, and children to have to make the impossible decision on whether to save her or her unborn child. I’m pro-little Cathy who had her innocence ripped away from her by someone she should have been able to trust and her 11 year old body isn’t mature enough to bear the consequence of that betrayal,” the Memiors of a Moddler post stated , before sharing several more scenarios. “You can argue and say that I’m pro-choice all you want, but the truth is: I’m pro-life. Burrow shared the post without adding any comment, allowing the post to speak for itself. Those comments came at a time when plenty of NFL players were hesitant to weigh in on political issues. And they put Burrow at odds with Vance, who has been a vocal opponent of abortion rights. Needless to say, Burrow probably wasn’t too broken up about missing his chance to meet the vice president. And with the Bengals set to face the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday, he likely has other things on his mind. item.description: KNOXVILLE, TN - SEPTEMBER 26: Linebacker Tyler Atkinson (16) of the Texas Longhorns looks on before the college football game against the Tennessee Volunteers on September 26, 2026 at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tennessee. That leaves wide receiver Kohen Brown as the other main contributor with his role on four special teams units. After the first two games of the season, when Brown only played on the kick coverage unit, Brown has been a mainstay on kick coverage, kick return, punt coverage, and punt return, totaling 91 snaps. Only seniors Ryan Niblett and Colton Vasek have played more snaps on special teams. Oddly enough, on Thursday Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian mentioned wide receiver Chris Stewart as a special teams contributor along with Brown even though Pro Football Focus hasn’t tracked any snaps for Stewart yet this season. “I see them every day. The way they work in practice, they are definitely showing up in that aspect of it, so I love love what they’re bringing,” Sarkisian said. The other freshmen mentioned by Sarkisian as making strides are all on defense — defensive linemen Jamarion Carlton and Brinley Tita, linebackers Tyler Atkinson and Rocky Cummings, and defensive backs Toray Davis and John Meredith III. That remains the case, but it’s notable that Sarkisian mentioned the Humble Summer Creek product. item.description: Hofmann double fires Leverkusen to third straight Europa League win Carles Martínez’s side scored both goals during a dominant spell in the first half, with Hofmann finding the net in the 35th and 37th minutes to put the visitors firmly in control. Leverkusen subsequently managed the game well to secure another three points and maintain their perfect start to the competition. Leverkusen initially had to be patient against an OFI side that started brightly in front of their home supporters. Both teams created opportunities during the opening stages, with goalkeepers at either end called into action to keep the score level. Hofmann came close to opening the scoring with a powerful effort from distance in the 19th minute, but OFI goalkeeper Lilo produced an impressive save. The hosts continued to threaten from set-pieces, although they struggled to turn their promising start into clear-cut opportunities. Leverkusen gradually grew into the contest and began to exploit the spaces between OFI’s defensive and midfield lines. Hofmann was denied again in the 31st minute, while Patrik Schick saw his follow-up effort cleared off the line after the home goalkeeper had initially saved. The breakthrough finally arrived in the 35th minute. Afonso Moreira unleashed a powerful shot from distance, and although Lilo managed to parry the effort, Hofmann reacted quickest to convert the rebound from close range. The German midfielder doubled his tally just two minutes later to put Leverkusen in a commanding position. item.title: Sergio Pérez talks about Cadillac’s present and future at the USGP

And while the results have not come overnight, the veteran driver believes that he and Bottas are doing getting everything they can out of the team’s package for the 2026 season, and even brighter days are ahead for the new kids on the block. “We’re not lacking anything on the driver’s side,” outlined Pérez to the media, including SB Nation, on Thursday at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin. “It’s really that once we get a little bit more performance, you know, once we close the gap a little bit more to the midfield, we will start [delivering results]. “The thing is that now we are overdelivering a lot as a team, but the car is just too far away.” Asked whether it was frustrating that the team was “overdelivering” but the results have not followed, Pérez highlighted his trust in the team and everyone involved with the project. “No, no, at the end of the day, my team understands it,” began Pérez. “People who really follow the sport well understand it, and more than anyone, myself, I go home happy when I know that I’ve done a good weekend, regardless of the results.” However, Pérez believes that 2027 will see the newest team on the grid take a big step forward, particularly with the car itself. “More to next year,” said Pérez when asked if a step forward was possible this season, or more likely in 2027. “Right now we are a new team, a smaller team. You are very limited with the budget cap, basically since we started the year. So, yeah, it’s more into next year.” As for what kind of step the team will take, Pérez is expecting something “big.” “We are expecting a big, a big step,” began Pérez. “I expect us to be making a very big step. That’s definitely the target. I think if we are able to do that, then we will be in a really good position to score points on a regular basis.” While the points may come on a regular basis in 2027, Pérez is set to celebrate a major F1 milestone earlier than that. item.title: Ryan Fitzpatrick doubles down on viral Broncos’ Bo Nix rant, except for 1 part
item.description: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Ryan Fitzpatrick doubles down on viral Broncos’ Bo Nix rant, except for 1 part appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Broncos are currently gearing up for their upcoming road game vs the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. The Broncos are coming off a home win over the Seattle Seahawks last week, in a game in which quarterback Bo Nix bizarrely refused to throw the ball downfield, although Denver still ended up getting the victory. After that contest, former NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick , who was an analyst for Prime’s coverage of the game, called Nix’s performance “almost disrespectful to the quarterback position.” Now, he has walked back those comments … kind of. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The line about being disrespectful to the quarterback position, it boiled over, and that’s the one phrase I wish I could have taken back, because I think my criticism was fair,” Fitzpatrick said, per Fitz & Whit, via Sam Neumann of Awful Announcing. “I don’t think the effort and the competitiveness that he’s shown in the past, I don’t think he was showing that at the end of the game. That is somewhere I usually don’t go, but that’s what I felt.” Indeed, many fans felt the phrasing crossed over into the personal realm, and it seems that Fitzpatrick has now acknowledged that mishap. Still, that doesn’t change the fact that the Broncos will need Nix to be much better and more aggressive in order to unlock the best version of themselves. The Broncos made a splashy move this offseason to go get wide receiver Jaylen Waddle in an effort to make life easier for Nix tossing the ball downfield, but that new dimension to the Denver offense has yet to materialize thus far. In any case, the Broncos will next hit the field on Sunday on the road vs the Cardinals. item.title: Mavericks' Kyrie Irving speaks on friendship with Texans' Azeez Al-Shaair, explains why he paid fine
item.description: Houston Texans linebacker Azeez al-Shaair (0) reacts after stopping Tennessee Titans running back Tony Pollard for a loss during the first half of an NFL football game in Nashville, Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026. (Brett Coomer/Houston Chronicle) Shortly after playing in his first NBA game in nearly 20 months due to injury, Kyrie Irving talked about his friendship with Houston Texans' captain Azeez Al-Shaair and his offer to pay the linebacker's fine from the NFL. "Azeez is a friend of mine," Irving said shortly after the Houston Rockets beat his Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday at Toyota Center. "He's a brother that I consider in this revolution that a lot of this generation is building." Al-Shaair and Irving have both been vocal in their support for Palestine during the conflict in Gaza. Al-Shaair was fined by the NFL for displaying the name Hind Rajab on his eye black during the Texans' season-opening loss in September . A week later, he was fined again when he wore the name Wafaa Akila on the black tape underneath his eyes during a loss to the Bengals. Rajab was a 5-year-old Palestinian girl killed during the Gaza war in 2024. Rajab was fleeing Gaza City with her family when their vehicle was attacked. While her uncle, aunt and cousins died, Rajab initially survived and was on the phone for hours with paramedics seeking rescue before she eventually died as well. Akila was an 8-year-old who who was killed during an Israeli airstrike while she was on her way to her first day of school in Gaza City earlier this year. When asked by ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime about his support for Al-Shaair, Irving praised his friend for his actions. "It's a selfless act when you can show up for others that don't necessarily have a voice for themselves," he said. "I would assume that most of us know what is happening around the world globally, and it's a lot of innocent people that are losing their lives, children, especially. Anytime there's a war or conflict, there's going to be unfortunate deaths and murders going on. And us here in America, we get the luxury of going to bed at night in our nice bedrooms and things paid for. But when our tax dollars are going towards things that we don't necessarily agree with, then you have to stand up. I think small instances of revolutionary acts like wearing people's names or wearing a child's name like Hind Rajab on your face and taking the fine and stepping up to the plate, it just shows how much you're an unselfish person, how much you're willing to sacrifice. item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Zach Charbonnet Returning In Week 7 Sinks Emanuel Wilson's Value
item.description: NFL Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After tearing his ACL in the NFC Championship Game back in late January, Seattle Seahawks running back Zach Charbonnet has been activated from the PUP list and is expected to make his season debut in Week 7. His presence will undoubtedly shake up the Seahawks' backfield. Zach Charbonnet (knee) was activated from the PUP list Thursday. Via @seahawksPR pic.twitter.com/UevCb9EuGH - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 22, 2026 Fantasy Impact RB Zach Charbonnet, Seattle Seahawks Charbonnet will return this week, but we have no idea how many snaps or touches he'll be able to handle in his first game back. It's more likely that he just muddies up the backfield and damages Emanuel Wilson, rather than Charbonnet being a startable fantasy football option himself in Week 7. When it comes to his long-term role, we'd expect that Charbonnet will lead a committee on the ground and handle the bulk of the goal-line work. This backfield could end up being a disaster for fantasy football owners with Charbonnet back and Jadarian Price working toward a return from injured reserve. RB Emanuel Wilson, Seattle Seahawks Wilson was already a shaky start this week in a tough matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs, but he is unstartable with Charbonnet back. The only thing Wilson had going for him was volume and touchdown upside. The return of Charbonnet will likely strip him of both those things. We would advise leaving Wilson on your bench this week, and he could be destined for the waiver wire in the near future. RB Jadarian Price, Seattle Seahawks Price's role in this offense is very much up in the air once he returns. While he was far more efficient than Wilson, he totaled just 119 yards in three games at 4.3 yards per carry. There is a real chance that the first-round pick returns as the RB2 in Seattle behind Charbonnet or in a near 50/50 split. We will have to play his rest-of-season value by ear. Nevertheless, it's unlikely he's a league-winner once he returns to action. item.title: Real Madrid star included in Champions League Team of the Week
item.description: Real Madrid star included in Champions League Team of the Week Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé has on Thursday seen his most recent exploits in European competition recognised. This comes courtesy of a place in the official UEFA Champions League Team of the Week. Frontman Mbappé is for his part fresh off another altogether productive outing on Wednesday night. Afforded a starting berth in Real Madrid’s Champions League meeting with German outfit RB Leipzig, the 27-year-old first laid on an assist for Arda Güler early in the 2nd-half. En route to an eventual 4-1 Blancos triumph, Mbappé then turned goalscorer late on, directing a wonderful right-footed strike into the far top corner from the edge of the Leipzig penalty area. And as alluded to above, a day on, such efforts have been aptly rewarded. Real Madrid’s top scorer has been included in the Champions League Team of the Week for Gameweek 3, joined by the likes of Harry Kane, Phil Foden and ex-Blancos talent Nico Paz: Conor Laird – GSFN

Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Scoring 28 points on 7-of-18 shooting and 5-for-12 from three-point range, Doncic led the way to the win while adding eight rebounds, dishing out seven assists and collecting three steals in less than 30 minutes of action. Simultaneously, Reaves finished with 23 points on 6-of-11 from the field and 1-for-3 from behind the three-point arc, registering four rebounds, six assists, two steals and a block to boot. Meanwhile, new addition Walker Kessler established himself in the paint, scoring 26 points on a perfect 12-for-12 from the field, grabbing nine rebounds while handing out an assist and finishing with two blocked shots. And that has the Lakers looking forward to seeing what their new Big Three can accomplish this season. UVA took a massive step forward in 2025 with Chandler Morris leading the Cavalier offense. The ‘Hoos were highly adaptable, scoring plenty points in shootouts against Florida State and Duke (in the regular season), but also controlling the ball and taking advantage of stout defensive performances against teams such as Washington State and Missouri. Despite losing players like Morris and J’Mari Taylor, and assistant coach Terry Heffernan to Stanford, the ‘Hoos entered 2026 with the most experienced offensive line in the country, an embarrassment of riches at running back, and the addition of Missouri transfer quarterback Beau Pribula. The formula for success for this offense seemed simple: Control the ball Lean on defenses with a diverse run game Take advantage of defensive mistakes through the air For the Virginia offense this year, sticking to this formula for a full sixty minutes has been much easier said than done. The 2026 Virginia offense has consistently started each game following this formula to letter. Virginia utilizes its talent up front to stay ahead of the chains, running backs Jekail Middlebrook and Xay Davis set the tone for the drive with consistent gains, and Pribula’s mobility is utilized not only as a runner but as a passer on designed rollouts that gain easy yards. Even the downfield passing game, seen as a potential weak spot on this team, is effectively utilized early, allowing Virginia to mix productive runs and chunk yardage to move the ball down the field and put points on the board. Starting fast is a skill in football, and more often than not, early points will put a team on the path to victory. In this effort, almost every team in college football will utilize a script of plays to be run in sequence to begin the game. This is done to set the tone for the offense, set up plays later in the game, and to determine the opponent’s defensive strategy. In this regard, Virginia has put on a masterclass in how to open up a football game, with early drives consistently putting points on the board for the ‘Hoos. The issues invariably begin for Virginia when the offense reaches the end of its opening script. Virginia will abandon schemes, players, and concepts that succeeded entirely, with the offense turning into a shell of itself. The once dynamic, fluid offense becomes decidedly rigid. This is best illustrated by Virginia’s percentage of drives that result in a score in each quarter against Power 4 opponents. SCORING DRIVE % VS. POWER 4 OPPONENTS % 1ST QUARTER 50% (6/12) 2ND QUARTER 17.65% (3/17) 3RD QUARTER 28.57% (4/14) 4TH QUARTER 33.33% (5/15) The drop-off in effectiveness is jarring to see, the Virginia offense has coin-flip odds of scoring in the 1st quarter, but struggles tremendously in the following three quarters. This would be a significant issue for any offense, but for an offense like Virginia’s, it can spell disaster. A ball-control offense that aims to dominate time of possession is going to have fewer chances to possess the football because they are taking more time off of the clock. To win while playing this style of football, Virginia can ill-afford to come away from possessions empty-handed this many times. The issue for this offense is not a lack of talent, a lack of will, or a rash of injuries. The issue at hand is one of implementation and feel for the game when defenses adjust to the initial script and we are forced to adjust in-game. This offense sees a clear shift in playcall selection and sequencing that coincides with the precipitous fall in offensive output. Blame for these offensive struggles has been widely placed with Virginia offensive coordinator and play-caller Des Kitchings. Kitchings’ 2025 campaign helped silence many doubters; however the first-half of the 2026 campaign has revived many of the concerns and criticisms surrounding his play-calling. Middlebrook was well on his way to another stellar game after 55 first half yards against SMU, but he only carried the ball twice in the second half for just 4 yards. Despite these issues, head coach Tony Elliott has been consistent in his support of Kitchings and it appears highly unlikely that he would make such a massive personnel change while his team possesses a winning record. After all, Elliott’s consistency and faith in his staff paid massive dividends in 2025 and has been a core principle of how he has rebuilt Virginia Football. That being said, it’s clear that Virginia’s offense must improve in order for the Cavaliers to make a bowl game, let alone put together the 8 to 10 win season many Virginia fans were hoping for. Though it may bring joy to the message boards and social media, I do not think that dismissing Des Kitchings is going to be a panacea for this offense. In fact, it could end up doing even greater harm than the current state of affairs is doing. Firing a coordinator is not only a massive change to make in the middle of the season, it can serve as a massive alarm bell to recruits, potential future members of the staff, and to the world that this is a program in crisis. While I would certainly call Virginia’s offensive struggles an area of great concern, the sky is not falling. We just need to score more points. Part of the solution for this problem might just be directing Kitchings’ efforts more towards what he does best, which is the preparation and game planing that goes on during the week prior to the game. When looking at that scoring drive chart from another angle, it’s very clear that Kitchings is highly effective in his preparation for the opposition and the ‘Hoos have a clear advantage with his early game scripting. It could be argued that the path to success for the Cavalier offense could come from letting Kitchings hone in on that rather than removing his play-calling responsibilities entirely. item.title: Liverpool find the sensational left-footer they need
item.description: Liverpool find the sensational left-footer they need Liverpool have their eyes locked on a left-footed star who could soon join. Can they get this over the line? Liverpool have a lot of attacking options right now. Tonnes, really, and arguably too many. Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike, Florian Wirtz, Dominik Szoboszlai, Bradley Barcola, Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz. It's a solid group with genuine world-class talent. However, none of them are left-footed. It's a bizarre trend at Liverpool where they only sign attacks who play off their right-foot. Even Yan Diomande, the first-choice summer signing, plays off his right. Liverpool could really use a left-footed player in attack, if only to change the angle of attack slightly. And they may have found one, even if he's very young. Liverpool consider move for Niko Ilicevic TeamTalk reports that Liverpool are one of the clubs in for Niko Ilicevic. The teenager is still only 15 but right on the verge of a first-team breakthrough and he's considered one of the biggest young talents in Germany. Eintracht Frankfurt are keen to tie him down to a long-term deal, of course, but clubs are hoping to turn his head. That includes Liverpool, who have been on a mission to find the best young talent around. Ilicevic could end up being the left-footed attacking star they need, too. No, he wouldn't break into the system immediately but with so many forwards at the club, it's unlikely that Liverpool sign someone for that group anyway. Instead, this would be for life after the current lot. Or life with Ngumoha, anyway, who looks set to be the star of the next generation. Now, it's difficult to know how likely Liverpool are to sign Ilicevic. He's a high-profile attacking player with the versatility to play across the forward line and scoring UEFA Youth League goals at 15. Those players are in high demand. Very high demand. It'll be an incredible battle to get him as a result - but one Liverpool clearly believe they can win.

item.title: Barcelona confirm Real Madrid El Clasico will go ahead despite workers’ strike
item.description: Barcelona confirm Real Madrid El Clasico will go ahead despite workers’ strike Barcelona have confirmed that Sunday’s La Liga clash against Real Madrid will take place as planned despite a three-day strike by seasonal workers at the club’s facilities, Mundo Deportivo reports. The strike is scheduled to begin at midnight on October 23 and end at 6:00 am on October 26, following a failed attempt to reach an agreement between the workers and the club at the Labour Court of Catalonia on Thursday. Around 60 seasonal workers are expected to take part in the industrial action to protest what they describe as a decline in their working conditions. Their concerns include a lack of staff to manage the various tasks required to organise sporting events across Barcelona’s facilities. Despite the planned protest, Barcelona insist they have enough resources to ensure all scheduled matches take place without changes. The club also made it clear that they would not use illegal methods to bring in replacement workers during the strike. The weekend’s biggest fixture is Sunday’s clash with Madrid , which is scheduled to kick off at 9:00 pm. The El Clasico is one of the most important matches on the Spanish football calendar, and any disruption would have raised concerns among supporters and organisers. However, the men’s first team will not be the only side affected by the strike. Barcelona have also confirmed that other professional teams will play their scheduled matches at the Spotify Camp Nou, Estadi Johan Cruyff and Palau Blaugrana. Youth team fixtures at the Ciutat Esportiva Joan Gamper will also go ahead as planned. The women’s first team are scheduled to host Granada in Liga F at the Estadi Johan Cruyff on Saturday at 8:30 pm. The men’s handball team will face Rebi Cuenca in the Liga Asobal on Friday at 7:00 pm. The club’s men’s basketball team will also be in action at the Palau Blaugrana, where they are scheduled to welcome Casademont Zaragoza in the Liga Endesa on Saturday at 9:00 pm. All these events fall within the strike period, leaving Barcelona to manage several major sporting occasions while dealing with workers’ complaints.

item.title: Angel Reese’s USA comments re-emerge amid national anthem snub
item.description: Photo by Nicholas Muller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images Many fans are still baffled by the ongoing walkoff before the national anthem in the WNBA finals. During the WNBA Finals, the national anthem drama blew up all over again. Players keep walking off the court before the song starts, brushing it off as just part of their normal pregame routine. But that hasn’t stopped people from calling out star players like Angel Reese, especially considering she just represented the country and brought home gold for USA Basketball. For a lot of fans watching, seeing someone suit up for Team USA one day and then skip the anthem the next just doesn’t sit right, no matter how routine the players claim it is. Angel Reese’s Team USA comments make it even more confusing Making the Team USA roster and bringing home World Cup gold was a big moment for Angel Reese . She called representing the country a dream come true and made it clear how much wearing that jersey means to her, while insisting she’ll never stop using her voice on the bigger issues. She said: “It’s an honor. To be one of 12, to be one of the best players in the U.S. and to be able to represent your country means a lot to me. It’s the dream that you want when you’re younger. It could have been anybody, and I’m just really happy I’m one of them.” It’s wild watching players like Angel Reese talk about how much of an honor it is to rep Team USA, only to turn around and duck off the court for the national anthem during WNBA games. And Riley Gaines is even suggesting they ban players who miss the national anthem from the upcoming Olympics, in an attempt to show some pride for the USA. item.title: Joao Cancelo hits back at critics after Barcelona’s defeat to PSG: ‘From the stands everyone is an expert’
item.description: Joao Cancelo hits back at critics after Barcelona’s defeat to PSG: ‘From the stands everyone is an expert’ Joao Cancelo has hit back at criticism of his performance in Barcelona’s 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain, posting a defiant message on Instagram just days before El Clasico against Real Madrid. The Portuguese full-back was heavily criticised after struggling defensively against PSG, particularly when Fabian Ruiz scored the home team’s fourth goal. With Barcelona preparing for another high-pressure match, Cancelo has made it clear that he believes judging players from the stands is easier than competing on the pitch. Cancelo challenges his critics after costly PSG performance “From the stands everyone is an expert. I want to see you get into the game and withstand the pressure,” Cancelo wrote in an Instagram story, accompanied by Michael Jackson’s ‘They Don’t Care About Us.’ Courtesy: Instagram He followed it with another post featuring a photograph of himself pointing towards the sky. Although Cancelo did not name anyone directly, the timing of the messages suggests a response to the backlash following Barcelona’s Champions League defeat. His performance at the Parc des Princes had placed him among the main targets of criticism, with supporters questioning his defensive positioning and decision-making. The Barcelona summer signing struggled to contain Desire Doue, received a yellow card in the first half and found it difficult to provide defensive security after switching flanks. His most damaging lapse came when he lost track of Ruiz, allowing the midfielder to score into an unguarded goal. Defensive concerns follow Cancelo into another major test The criticism has revived questions about Cancelo’s reliability in high-stakes matches. His attacking instincts and ability to advance down the flank offer Barcelona a useful weapon, but his defensive positioning can leave the team exposed when opponents exploit space behind him. Facing criticism. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) There is also an uncomfortable precedent. During Barcelona’s Champions League quarter-final against PSG in April 2024, Cancelo was criticised for his defensive mistakes as the Catalans exited the competition. His latest performance has brought those concerns back into focus . Manager Hansi Flick continues to value the Portuguese defender’s attacking contribution, and Barcelona may need him again against Real Madrid, particularly with options in defence limited by injuries. That leaves the manager balancing Cancelo’s ability to create danger going forward against the risk of leaving space for opponents to exploit. Amidst all this, Cancelo’s Instagram posts show that he is aware of the criticism surrounding his performance in Paris. But while his frustration with outside judgement is understandable, the upcoming meeting with Real Madrid gives him a more immediate way to change the conversation.

item.title: Report: Rival team has threatened Red Wings with Simon Edvinsson offersheet
item.description: Report: Rival team has threatened Red Wings with Simon Edvinsson offersheet The Detroit Red Wings could be facing another major test in their efforts to keep their young defensive core together, and this time, the Carolina Hurricanes may be the team applying the pressure. According to Elliotte Friedman on the latest episode of the 32 Thoughts podcast, he believes Carolina has threatened to pursue an offer sheet for Red Wings defenseman Simon Edvinsson. If that threat becomes reality, Detroit could find itself facing a difficult decision involving one of its most important young players. Edvinsson, who has emerged as a significant part of Detroit's defensive plans, represents exactly the type of player rebuilding teams cannot afford to lose without carefully considering the long-term consequences. The towering Swedish defenseman brings size, mobility, and considerable upside, making him an attractive target for a Hurricanes organization that has consistently looked for ways to strengthen its roster. For Detroit, the timing could hardly be more uncomfortable. The Red Wings have invested considerable time and resources into developing their young talent, and Edvinsson is the kind of defenseman they would presumably prefer to keep in the fold as they attempt to become a legitimate Stanley Cup contender. The biggest concern for Detroit is that this situation has already dragged into the regular season. item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US in South Florida on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage On Thursday, Concacaf announced that it had approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Initially, Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the United States, had been booked in Kingston. The Grenadiers had previously played their World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . item.content:encoded: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
